description: Stereo phaser of four or six stages, first or second order, swept by a modulator of its own or by a voltage from outside

params.text: The rate of the built in modulator
How far the built in modulator sweeps the phaser
The resonance of the phaser stages
How wide the band the phaser sweeps across is; the row of lamps shows it between 20Hz and 10kHz
Where the swept band is centred, between 20Hz and 10kHz as shown by the row of lamps
Six phaser stages in the 6 position and four in the 4 position
Second order stages in the 2 position and first order stages in the 1 position
Chooses the shape of the built in modulator, shown by the lamp above the shape: sine, triangle, sawtooth or square
Takes the phaser out of the signal path, so the input passes straight to the output
The balance between the untreated signal and the phased signal

inputs.text: The left side of the stereo input
A voltage here sweeps the phaser in place of its own modulator
A voltage moving the rate of the built in modulator
A voltage moving the sweep of the built in modulator
A voltage moving the DEPTH setting
A voltage moving the width of the swept band
A voltage moving the centre of the swept band
The right side of the stereo input
A trigger switches the bypass on and off

outputs.text: The left side of the stereo output
The right side of the stereo output
